info.title: Mimiry Organizations API
info.description:
Organization management API for the Mimiry platform. Create and manage
organizations, invite members, and control access.

## Authentication

All endpoints require a JWT Bearer token obtained via SSH signature exchange
(`POST /api/auth/v1/token`) or portal login.

## Async Operations

Mutating operations (create, update, delete, invite, etc.) return
`202 Accepted` with a `request_id` and a `status_url`. Poll the status
endpoint, or stream it, to learn the outcome: the `202` means the request
was accepted, not that it succeeded. A status is kept for 15 minutes.

```
POST /api/organizations/v1 → 202 { request_id, status_url }
GET  /api/organizations/v1/operations/{request_id} → { status: "completed" }
```

## Roles in an organization

| Role | What it allows |
|------|----------------|
| **owner** | Everything below, plus changing members' roles, transferring ownership, winding down and deleting the organization. |
| **admin** | Changing the organization's name and slug; inviting members; removing members other than the owner; revoking invitations. |
| **member** | Reading the organization, its members and its pending invitations. Leaving. |

Operations marked **(requires elevated rights)** need one of these rights in
the organization. Without it the answer is `403`.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete organizations.

post.description:
Creates a new organization. The authenticated user becomes the owner.
Ordinary accounts may create organizations; an account that exists only
to join organizations it is invited to may not, and gets `403`.

The slug must be globally unique and is used in URLs. It is normalized
to lowercase and must start with `o-`, followed by 1–32 lowercase
letters, digits and single hyphens (not at either end). A slug without
the prefix is rejected with `400 invalid_slug`.

Returns `202 Accepted`: the organization is created asynchronously.
Poll the `status_url`; on completion its `result.organization` is the
new organization.

403.description: This account may not create organizations.

example.message: Your account type does not allow creating organizations

409.description:
The slug is taken (`slug_exists`), or another request is claiming
it right now (`slug_pending`, retry).

example.message: An organization with this slug already exists

get.description:
Returns the organizations the authenticated user owns or is a member of,
one page at a time.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Field to sort by. `role` is the caller's role in each organization.
An unknown field is refused with `400`.

get.description: Returns the organization and its members. Members only.

patch.description:
Changes the organization's name or slug. The owner or an admin may.
Only the fields given are changed.

403.description: The caller is not the owner or an admin.

example.message: Only owner or admin can update organization

delete.description:
Deletes the organization. Only the owner may. This cannot be undone.

Deletion is refused while the organization has other members or
invitations that can still be accepted; the operation then ends
`failed` and its `error` names what is in the way. To retire an
organization that still has members, wind it down first.

403.description: The caller is not the owner.

example.message: Only the owner can delete an organization

post.summary: Start winding down an organization (requires elevated rights)
post.description:
Starts retiring the organization. Only the owner may.

A wind-down freezes the organization: no new members, invitations,
sessions or volumes. Members keep read access for `readable_days`,
after which the organization can be deleted. Volumes are kept for
`volume_grace_days` and are billed until then.

Whether the caller is the owner is decided when the request is
processed, so a refusal arrives as a `failed` operation.

400.description: A bound is out of range.

example.message: readable_days is required (1-90); volume_grace_days must be 0-30

delete.description:
Ends a wind-down and unfreezes the organization. Only the owner may;
a refusal arrives as a `failed` operation.

get.description:
Returns the organization by slug. Members only. The slug is normalized
to lowercase.

Lists the organization's members, oldest first (by `joined_at`). Members
only.

patch.summary: Change a member's role (requires elevated rights)
patch.description:
Changes a member's role to `admin` or `member`. Only the owner may.
Nobody can change their own role or the owner's; ownership moves with
transfer-ownership instead.

400.description: An unknown role, or the caller's own or the owner's role.

example.message: Cannot change the owner's role

403.description: The caller is not the owner.

example.message: Only organization owner can change member roles

404.description: No such organization, or the user is not a member of it.

example.message: Member not found in organization

delete.description:
Removes a member. The owner or an admin may remove anyone but the
owner. Any member may remove themselves, which is how to leave an
organization.

example.message: Cannot remove organization owner

403.description: The caller may not remove this member.

example.message: You don't have permission to remove this member

post.description:
Hands the organization to another member. Only the owner may, and the
new owner must already be a member.

Both are decided when the request is processed, so a refusal arrives
as a `failed` operation.

400.description: `new_owner_id` is missing or not a UUID.

example.message: new_owner_id is required and must be a UUID

get.description:
Lists the organization's invitations that can still be accepted:
pending and not expired. Members only.

503.description:
The invitations could not be read. This is not a statement that
there are none. Retry.

example.message: Could not read invitations; this is not a statement that there are none. Retry.

post.description:
Invites someone by email address or by username: exactly one of the
two. The owner or an admin may.

The role is `admin` or `member`. An invitation can be accepted for
7 days.

400.description: Neither or both of `email` and `username`, or an unknown role.

example.message: Exactly one of 'email' or 'username' is required

403.description: The caller is not the owner or an admin.

example.message: You don't have permission to invite members

404.description: No such organization, or no user with that username.

example.message: No user with that username

delete.description:
Withdraws a pending invitation, so it can no longer be accepted. The
owner or an admin may. An invitation that is no longer pending is not
changed, and the operation ends `failed`.

403.description: The caller is not the owner or an admin.

example.message: Only the organization owner or an admin can revoke an invitation

get.description:
Says whether the caller may accept the invitation, before they try.
Acceptance itself is decided when it is processed; this is a preview.

A caller the invitation is not addressed to learns only that:
`can_accept` is false with a `reason`, and nothing about the
organization. The invitee also gets the organization, the role and
the expiry.

200.description: The verdict, and the details for the invitee.

example.message: Invitation not found or no longer valid

503.description: The invitation could not be read right now.

example.message: Could not verify this invitation right now

post.description:
Accepts an invitation with the token from the invitation email. It must
be addressed to the caller: their account, or their email address. A
refusal arrives as a `failed` operation.

get.description:
Returns the status of an asynchronous operation. Poll this endpoint
after receiving a `202 Accepted` response.

Answers `202` while pending, and `200` when completed or failed. A
status is kept for 15 minutes.

example.message: Operation not found or expired

bearerAuth.description:
JWT token obtained via SSH signature exchange (`POST /api/auth/v1/token`)
or portal login (`POST /api/auth/v1/login`).

Include in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

InvitationToken.name: token
InvitationToken.description: The token from the invitation email.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Clamped to [1, 100]; defaults to 50.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Number of items to skip from the start of the (sorted) result set.

RequestId.name: request_id
RequestId.description: Unique identifier of the asynchronous operation.

Accepted.description: Accepted for processing. Poll `status_url` for the outcome.

NotAMember.description: The caller is not a member of the organization.

example.message: Access denied
Organization not found

Unavailable.description: Whether the request is allowed could not be determined right now. Retry.

example.message: The request could not be completed right now. Retry.
Invalid request body
Authentication required
Internal server error

owner_name.description: The owner's display name. In list answers only.

Invitation.description:
An invitation that can still be accepted. It is addressed to an email
address or to an account, so one of `email` and `invited_user_id` is
set.

reason.description: Why the caller cannot accept. Absent when they can.

message.example: This invitation was sent to a different email address

org_id.description: For the invitee only, as are the fields below.

slug.description:
URL-safe identifier, normalized to lowercase: `o-` followed by 1–32
lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. A few bodies are
reserved (for example `admin`).
A new slug, by the same rules as at creation.

email.description: The invitee's email address. Give this or `username`.

username.description: The invitee's username. Give this or `email`.

new_owner_id.description: Must already be a member of the organization.

readable_days.description: How long members keep read access before the organization can be deleted.

drain_sessions.description: Let running sessions finish instead of ending them.

volume_grace_days.description:
Keep volumes this many days. They are billed until then, and the
grace cannot be longer than `readable_days`.

ErrorResponse.description:
Every error from the public API has this shape. Branch on `error`, never on
`message`: the code is part of the API, while the sentence may be reworded.
Some errors carry more fields beside these two; each operation documents
its own.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence a person can read.

example.message: Organization name is required

AsyncResponse.description: Response returned when an operation is accepted for asynchronous processing.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for tracking this operation.

message.description: Human-readable description of the accepted operation.

status_url.description: URL to poll for operation status updates.

retry_after.description: Suggested number of seconds before polling for status.

example.message: Request accepted and is being processed

result.description: Operation result data (present when status is "completed").
